title: SDK error contract: unify codes, exceptions, and streaming error envelopes across Py/TS/Go
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a single error surface and developer ergonomics for the three official SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) so that errors are predictable, actionable, and instrumentable across runtimes. This ticket covers spec, prototype implementations, tests, docs, and rollout plan.

Motivation:
- Customers across languages report inconsistent error shapes and messaging; cross-team incident response and support are slowed because codes/messages differ.
- Retries and streaming clients need clear guidance from SDKs about which failures are transient vs permanent.
- Console and monitoring need stable error codes for aggregation and alerting.

Scope / non-goals:
- Include: error code taxonomy, canonical string and numeric codes, mapping to HTTP statuses, client-side exception classes/types, retryability semantics, streaming error envelope design, SDK examples, migration path, tests, CI checks, and telemetry keys.
- Exclude: server-side error formatting changes outside the inference API (separate infra ticket). If server shape cannot be changed immediately, SDKs will adapt with translation layers.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published: canonical error taxonomy (name, numeric code, category, default HTTP mapping, retryable flag, human message) in SDK RFC
Python/TS/Go SDKs include language-native error types that expose .code / Code() and .retryable / IsRetryable() and stable string codes
Streaming protocol: error frames standardized (fields: code, message, retriable, details) and SDK stream iterators yield a typed StreamError event before raising final exception
Retry test harness: unit/integration tests asserting retry wrapper respects retryable flag across SDKs
Backcompat: existing SDKs continue to parse older error shapes for at least one release with logging warnings and migration guidance
Telemetry: server + client emit stable metric label `redwood_error_code` and use numeric code for metrics aggregation
design_notes:
Core proposals: 
1) Error taxonomy: CATEGORY_CODE naming (e.g., AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, MODEL_TIMEOUT, KVCACHE_MISS_UNAVAILABLE). Assign stable numeric values in a reserved range (1000..1999 for client errors, 2000..2999 for transient/server errors, 3000..3999 for platform/throttling).
2) Error fields: { code: string, numeric_code: int, message: string, retriable: boolean, details: optional dict } -- SDKs will expose `details` as dict/map typed in each language.
3) Python ergonomics: exception base class RedwoodError(Exception) with attributes `code: str`, `numeric_code: int`, `retriable: bool`, and helper methods `is_retryable()`, `to_dict()`; specific subclasses created for common categories (AuthError, RateLimitError, TransientError).
4) TypeScript ergonomics: export enum ErrorCode and class RedwoodError extends Error { code: ErrorCode | string; numericCode: number; retriable: boolean; details?: Record<string, any> }. Provide typed guards `isRetryable(err)`.
5) Go ergonomics: sentinel typed error values and an interface RedwoodError { Error() string; Code() string; NumericCode() int; Retryable() bool; Details() map[string]interface{} } plus helper functions `IsRetryable(err error)`. Use errors.Is wrapping for comparisons.
6) Retries: SDKs should include a default retry policy that only retries codes flagged retriable (e.g., 2001 TRANSIENT_BACKEND_ERROR, 3001 THROTTLE_BACKOFF). Policy parameters configurable by developer.
7) Streaming: each stream message envelope may include an `error` object that mirrors top-level error fields. Streaming iterators must yield a `StreamError` event that contains code and retriable flag and then close/raise according to protocol. Partial outputs before stream errors must be surfaced to caller as well.
8) Backcompat: implement translation adapters that map existing server error payloads to the canonical model until servers ship the new shape. SDKs log deprecation warnings when translation occurs.
implementation_plan: 1) Draft RFC + example payloads and a small JSON schema for the error shape. 2) Create prototype in python SDK: RedwoodError class, adapter for server shapes, unit tests. 3) Mirror API in TypeScript SDK + examples. 4) Implement Go interface and adapt libraries. 5) Add stream error envelope support to streaming client implementations. 6) Add telemetry mapping and CI check that prevents new regression (server PRs must include code mapping). 7) Rollout: opt-in flag in SDKs for 2 releases, then enabled-by-default. 8) Post-rollout: update console and docs.
risks_and_mitigations: Server adoption lag: mitigation - adapter/translation layer in SDKs and shipping deprecation warnings
Breaking changes for users depending on message text: mitigation - preserve raw_message and include 'legacy_message' field in translated errors
Overbroad retry rules causing repeated failures: mitigation - initial default is conservative; encourage explicit override; add telemetry to detect retry storms
Streaming semantics complexity: mitigation - provide clear iterator APIs and examples for both 'raise-on-first-error' and 'deliver-partial-then-error' behaviors

review_feedback: PM Priya: prefer string codes as primary identifier in logs for readability; numeric codes used in metrics. Agreed - SDK exposes both.
Security: avoid leaking internal debug info in public messages. Decision: `details` is optional and may be stripped by default; SDKs expose raw_details only when `debug=True` in client config.
DevRel Evan: request concise examples for streaming error handling in docs; added examples folder and sample apps.
